I won't get over it, because the spread of misinformation surrounding GMO products could potentially be incredibly harmful to public health. If consumers refuse to purchase GMO products so that producers selling them, then our food supply would become susceptible to devastation. Say we stop using GMO corn only to get hit with a corn blight -- the prices for every single food product would skyrocket. All animal products depend on corn, so meat, dairy, poultry, and fish prices would go up. Basically every food you buy at a store somehow involves corn in its production. Even foods that have nothing to do with corn, like tomatoes for example, would grow far more expensive, because supply would suddenly fall way short of demand as a result of the market being forced to shift to other foods.

Net result? The poor wouldn't be able to afford any nutritious food, causing severe health issues, as if they needed any more dietary problems. The middle class would undergo significant economic strain to keep healthy food on the table, resulting in a myriad of fiscal issues that may prevent businesses from going, people going to college, people being able to afford health care, etc. Meanwhile, the wealthy would probably be fine, so there's that. Consumer choice is fantastic, but spreading disinformation and playing with public health as an attempt to stick it to certain companies is irresponsible and reprehensible.

All that said, I acknowledge problems in the food industry. We need more diversity in the kinds of foods we eat, more sustainable farming practices, increased biosecurity, less environmentally damaging chemicals, and generally more nutritious diets, but those are completely different issues.
